title: Anisotropic product noise operator
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $\{\phi_a:a\in\iota\}$ be an orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ for the $\pi$-weighted inner product, indexed by a finite nonempty set $\iota$. Suppose one basis vector, indexed by $a_0$, is the constant-one function. Given a function $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$ and real coordinate parameters $\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_n$, its anisotropic product noise transform at $x\in\Omega^n$ is the sum over product-basis indices $a\in\iota^n$ of the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $a$ times the product-basis function at $x$, weighted by the product of $\rho_j$ over coordinates $j$ for which $a_j\ne a_0$.
hypotheses_covered: Orthonormal basis of functions on $\Omega$ for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
A basis vector indexed by $a_0$ is constant one
